conviction_note: New Q3 numbers with no company guidance to move: abs 7% from the European 'numbers new' base and HANZA's own observed report-day moves (median ~5%, recent +15%, +26%, -0.9%). p_up 48, a hair under 50: all three Nordic EMS peers that reported in the past four days fell 6.5-11% on their prints, two of them citing tight component availability and inventory-driven cash weakness. Against that, HANZA has already fallen ~8% in sympathy, the one sourced preview (SB1) sits above consensus on EBITA, and HANZA's own prints have mostly been bought. The findings sum (-0.5) and the scaled number (-0.28) agree in sign and are both close to zero, which is the honest result.

findings.finding: Two of HANZA's closest Nordic EMS peers reported Q3 in the last four days with tight component availability and inventory-driven weak cash flow. NOTE: organic growth only 2%, held back by material availability, operating cash flow 11 MSEK vs 121. Scanfil: 'component availability required increased focus', operating cash flow EUR 4.1m vs 7.4m. HANZA itself flagged in Q2 that component supply 'remains uncertain' for H2, so its Q3 organic growth and cash flow carry the same risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HANZA's misses on organic growth were sold. Report days 2024-02-13 (-5.5%) and 2024-05-07 (-2.8%) came in a weak-demand phase, while strong-organic prints (2025-05-06 +10.6%, 2026-05-05 +26.0%) were bought hard. Cash flow has not been a known swing line for this name.
findings.original_quote: Vår tillväxt i perioden hålls tillbaka av en lägre tillgänglighet för vissa material samt produktionsstörningar under perioden kopplade till fabriksflyttar i två verksamheter. [...] Det mer ansträngda materialläget har inneburit en betydande lageruppbyggnad för att säkerställa materialtill[gång] (Our growth in the period is held back by lower availability of certain materials and by production disruptions tied to factory moves in two operations. [...] The tighter material situation has meant a significant inventory build to secure material supply.)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: HANZA fell 3.2% on NOTE/Scanfil day and 6.1% on Kitron day, 8% over five sessions. If it were fully priced the sell-side bar would have moved, and SB1's above-consensus EBITA preview from 8 Oct still stands with no later preview revision found. This is a peer proxy, not a HANZA number, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Scanfil Q3, a different issuer and document: 'The operating environment remained challenging, as component availability required increased focus and dedication', with operating cash flow of EUR 4.1m. https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b1383c083bd04923ff3f607a3c6d4f830&lang=en&src=listed. HANZA's own Q2 warning: https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/afe1e359da0865fe83ede78a37813d37b

findings.finding: This season the sector's reaction function is selling prints. All three Nordic EMS peers fell on their Q3 day: Kitron -10.1% on 22 Oct with record backlog and an unchanged guide but sequential revenue down from EUR 296m to 267m; NOTE -11.0% on 23 Oct; Scanfil -6.5% on 23 Oct despite 8.5% organic growth and a release titled 'Strong Customer Wins'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HANZA's own prints have mostly been bought regardless of peers: +16.5% (Q3 2024), +4.8% (Q3 2025), +15.1% (Q4 2025), +26.0% (Q1 2026), -0.9% (Q2 2026, when Kitron's Q2 had fallen 11% two weeks earlier). That history is why this finding is small.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: HANZA already took the sympathy hit (-8% in five sessions, from 166 to ~154). What is not priced is whether the market applies the same 'sell the print' treatment to HANZA's own numbers on the day. In Q2 it did not (-0.9%) after Kitron's Q2 fell 11%.
findings.independence: Prices from Yahoo: KIT.OL 95.05 to 85.45 on 2026-10-22, NOTE.ST 173.2 to 154.1 on 2026-10-23, SCANFL.HE 12.84 to 12.00 on 2026-10-23 (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NOTE.ST?range=1mo&interval=1d). These are price data, not an independent fundamental source.

findings.finding: SB1 Markets' preview (8 Oct) puts Q3 EBITA at 200 MSEK, 5.3% above consensus, on rising volumes and better profitability at the acquired BMK, with organic growth of 9.5%. This matches the company's own Q2 statement that BMK's margin rose from 7.3% to 7.5% and will 'continue to improve', and that comparable-unit margin was 9.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin beats have been HANZA's big up-days: Q1 2026 +26.0% and Q4 2025 +15.1%.
findings.original_quote: Omsättningen väntas bli 2 374 miljoner kronor, 2 procent under konsensus, medan ebita väntas bli 200 miljoner kronor, 5,3 procent över konsensus. Stigande volymer och förbättrad lönsamhet inom förvärvade BMK väntas lyfta marginalerna. (Sales are expected at SEK 2,374m, 2% below consensus, while EBITA is expected at SEK 200m, 5.3% above consensus. Rising volumes and better profitability at the acquired BMK are expected to lift margins.)
findings.why_not_priced: This is on the wire, so mostly priced. It sits inside what the company itself steered to (BMK margin improving), so it is sized near zero. It survives as a small positive only because the stock has since fallen ~8% on peers while this estimate was not withdrawn.
findings.independence: HANZA's Q2 report CEO letter: 'we expect ... that HANZA BMK's operating margin will continue to improve.' https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/afe1e359da0865fe83ede78a37813d37b

findings.finding: Positive demand read-through from peers with the same end markets. Scanfil reported 8.5% organic growth with 'a strong finish' to the quarter. Kitron reported growth 'broader' than defence, with electrification 'where the change is clearest', and backlog up 41%. Electrification & Energy (22%) and Defence (8%) are HANZA segments.
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer demand statements, and the market read the peer days negatively overall (all three fell), so the demand half of the read-through was arguably discarded with the supply half. It is a proxy for HANZA's mix (heavy mechanics, mining, BMK electronics), so it is sized small and net of the 45% of HANZA revenue in industrial machinery and professional products, where Q2 sales were stable or declining.
findings.independence: Kitron Q3 release, 2026-10-22: 'In the third quarter, growth was broader. Electrification is where the change is clearest.' https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=684562
